frontier.hypothesis: out2's missing fourth reference exists as an insn that survives cse1 and flow and is then absorbed by combine — the same shape E-s16-5 proved target's own stptr reference has — and the way to find it is to enumerate combine's merge patterns rather than to keep guessing C spellings.
frontier.mechanism: combine.c's try_combine runs AFTER flow.c has counted reg_n_refs, so a reference living in an insn combine later absorbs is both counted and byte-free. The candidate consumers are target's own block-2 insns (addiu $s1/$s2,0x6C; addiu $s4,zero,0x12; lw $t0,0x18($sp); addiu $s3,$s7,0x20; addiu $s0,$t0,0x750) and its block-0 tail. This is the only clause-satisfying shape left after E-s21-5 (flow deletion is uncounted) and E-s22-2 (chain-extenders need a dying donor).

E-s20-2). Rule out in advance anything arithmetically collapsible before combine sees it — cse1 reassociates those (E-s20-3).

frontier.mechanism: A1 has a3 4 refs / live 99 = 808 immediately above a4 7/190 = 736 and out2 3/42 = 714. a3's priority is floor_log2(4)*4/live*10000, so a3 drops below 736 at live >= 109 and below 714 at live >= 114. Target order is out2 > a4 > a3 while A1 has a3 > a4 > out2, so a3 must fall two places — check whether a4 must be lifted at the same time (a4 reaches 1263 at 8 references, which is what the block-0 wrap buys today).
